newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount, Paz buy Mondex Israel rights.
newsitem.headline: Discount, Paz buy Mondex Israel rights.

text.p: Israel's Discount Investment Corp and Paz Oil Co said on Monday they had purchased the Mondex electronic cash franchise rights for Israel.
The companies declined to disclose the sum paid for the rights.

Mondex is a payment smartcard being introduced by banks and retailers around the world as an alternative to cash. It allows banks to transfer electronic cash to and from customers via phone systems and automated teller machines. It also can be used for shopping and for person-to-person payments.

In contrast to other Mondex franchise operators Discount Investment and Paz will develop Mondex with partners from banking, industry and the retail communities to ensure widespread acceptance, the companies said in a statement.
The group plans to introduce Mondex in Israel in the first quarter of 1998. A Mondex spokeswoman in Tel Aviv said the companies intend to charge a small annual fee for use of the card.

"Israelis have a reputation for embracing new technology and I am confident Mondex will quickly become a part of everyday life throughout the country," Discount Investments managing director Dov Tadmor said.

London-based Mondex International Ltd is an independent payments company that is majority owned by MasterCard International in addition to 27 other major organisations in Europe, North America, Australia and Asia.

Discount Investment, a subsidiary of IDB Holdings Ltd, is one of Israel's largest investment companies with assets approaching $1 billion. Its holdings inlcude Supersol ltd, Israel's biggest food retailer, and Cellcom, which operates the country's largest cellular phone network.
Paz is Israel's largest supplier of refined petroleum products and its largest petroleum retailer.
